name: PhpCodeArcheology

hlido_opinion.headline: A PHP static-analysis tool that measures architecture rather than just style — 60+ metrics, 14 problem detectors and six output formats — and is, by its own claim, the first PHP analyzer with a native MCP server and a generated CLAUDE.md.
hlido_opinion.body: PhpCodeArcheology positions itself past the linter tier: 60+ architecture and maintainability metrics (cyclomatic and cognitive complexity, maintainability index, LCOM, Halstead, instability, coupling, type coverage) computed per file, class, method and function, plus 14 problem detectors (god classes, dead code, circular dependencies, deep inheritance) flagged with error/warning/info severity and actionable descriptions. It is MIT, PHP 8.2–8.5, composer-installed, needs no extensions, and — unusually for this category — is framework-aware, reading composer.json to detect Symfony/Laravel/Doctrine and adjust thresholds so framework boilerplate does not generate false positives. Two features make it genuinely agent-relevant and lift the score: it ships a native MCP server (it claims to be the first PHP static-analysis tool with one) so an assistant can query hotspots, dependency graphs and refactoring priorities in natural language, and it generates a CLAUDE.md project overview an AI assistant can read before touching the code. The six output formats include SARIF for GitHub Code Scanning and a JSON path for CI, so it slots into existing pipelines. The honest limits: it is PHP-only by design, the '60+/14/first-with-MCP' figures are the project's own claims rather than independently benchmarked here, and self-authored metric thresholds are still self-authored. Within PHP, this is a thorough, transparent and unusually agent-forward analyzer.

tier_rationale: STEADY (77) because PhpCodeArcheology is a thorough, transparent architecture analyzer (60+ metrics with a formula glossary, 14 detectors, six formats incl. SARIF), is framework-aware to avoid false positives, and is genuinely agent-native — a native MCP server plus a generated CLAUDE.md. Held at 77 because it is PHP-only by design, the headline counts and 'first-with-MCP' claim are self-reported rather than benchmarked here, and its thresholds are self-authored.
what_it_does_well: 60+ architecture/maintainability metrics per file/class/method/function, with a glossary of formulas and thresholds
14 problem detectors (god classes, dead code, circular dependencies, deep inheritance) with severity and actionable descriptions
Native MCP server — query hotspots, dependency graphs and refactoring priorities in natural language
Generates a CLAUDE.md project overview for an AI coding assistant to read first
Six output formats including SARIF for GitHub Code Scanning and JSON for CI
Framework-aware: reads composer.json (Symfony/Laravel/Doctrine) and adjusts thresholds to cut false positives
MIT, PHP 8.2–8.5, composer-installed, no extensions required; test-coverage integration (PHPUnit/Pest/Codeception)
what_it_fails_at: PHP-only by design — no value for other languages
Headline figures (60+ metrics, 14 detectors, 'first PHP tool with native MCP') are project claims, not benchmarked here
Metric thresholds are self-authored, as with any single-vendor analyzer
Depth on very large legacy codebases is asserted rather than demonstrated on the reviewed surface
best_for: PHP teams maintaining long-lived codebases who need architecture and maintainability metrics, not just style checks
Engineers who want an AI assistant to query codebase health and refactoring priorities over MCP
CI pipelines that consume SARIF (GitHub Code Scanning) or JSON alongside architecture reports
not_recommended_for: Teams that only need a fast style linter rather than architecture metrics

compared_to.verdict_diff: Sonarly is a general code-quality/analysis play; PhpCodeArcheology is PHP-specific, architecture-focused (LCOM, coupling, instability) and ships a native MCP server plus a generated CLAUDE.md. Sonarly for broad quality, PhpCodeArcheology for deep PHP architecture with agent-native querying.

Serena is a multi-language semantic code toolkit for navigation/editing; PhpCodeArcheology measures PHP architecture health and exposes it over MCP. Serena for cross-language structural operations, PhpCodeArcheology for PHP metrics and refactoring priorities.

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: Two agent paths: a native MCP server the assistant queries in natural language for hotspots, dependency graphs, health scores and refactoring priorities (MCP tool calls such as get_hotspots and get_refactoring priorities), and a generated CLAUDE.md the assistant reads before editing the codebase. Also runs as a composer-installed CLI producing JSON/SARIF for CI. Directly designed for AI-assisted PHP maintenance.
